_doc: The economy mod's match (#524): a stocked economy and a town of wood, planks and stone. Serfs carry and build; only woodcutters and stone cutters, trained at the school, gather, each at its hut. One age; no soldiers. After the opening tips come the town's goals (#104).

cost._doc: the school's fee: every trade costs 10 gold to teach, smelted at the gold smelter (#116; it was food, which nothing here makes). One age, so its gold isn't paid in food as the base rules' age 1 would.

tips.text: With nothing selected, press Build: Civilian and lay a School. Your serfs bring the goods and build it.
Lay a Woodcutter's Hut near trees. Serfs build it; a woodcutter will work there.
When the School is built, click it and train a Woodcutter: it walks to the hut and starts cutting.
Your people eat bread and sausages. Lay a Farm, a Mill and a Bakery, and train a Farmer, a Miller and a Baker at the School.
Grow the town to 15 people: train serfs and trades at the School.
tips.label: Goal

tips.text: Lay an Iron Mine and a Coal Mine with their backs to the seams in the mountain, and train Miners.
tips.label: Goal

tips.text: Smelt your first iron at an Iron Smelter: it takes iron ore and coal.
tips.label: Goal

tips.text: Forge 10 tools at the Smithy. Stone cutters, farmers, millers and bakers need them to start work.
tips.label: Goal

tips.text: Feed the town sausages too: lay a Pig Farm and a Butcher, and make 30 sausages.
tips.label: Goal

tips.text: Smelt 20 gold at a Gold Smelter.
tips.label: Goal

roads._doc: the genre's road (#138): no quicker to walk (a serf walks 1 tile a second anywhere), but paths keep to it (crossing it costs a third of open ground), walked tile to tile down its middle, and two passing on it trade places instead of shoving
roads.name: road

hunger._doc: life: seconds a full bar lasts; hungry_at: the seconds left when they go to eat; start_pct, jitter_pct: a new one's bar, give or take (the genre's: 45 min, 6 min, 60 and 10); eaters: the slots that eat; starving_pct: how much a hungry worker with nowhere to eat works, none once the bar is empty; foods: what's eaten, the most filling first, with the share of the bar each fills (the genre's: sausages 60, fish 50, bread 40, wine 30); eat_secs: how long one food takes at the inn's table (the mod's hooks/hunger.lua, #47, #132)

start._doc: a storehouse stocked to get going (Dominic, 2026-11-20, #119): goods for the first buildings and their roads, some late goods (tools, iron, coal, sausages) and gold enough to pay the school till the gold smelter does

gather_ticks._doc: planks, flour and bread are made, never gathered; every resource needs a rate. The raw trades at the genre's pace (#139): a trunk felled in 30 s, a stone cut in 15 s, ore and coal dug in 35 s, one at a time

economy._tools_doc: tools_for: the trades that take a tool from a store before they start at a workplace (the mod's hooks/jobs.lua, #102). The wood and metal trades bring their own, so a town with no tools left can always make more.

+roster.name: Serf
+roster.desc: Carries goods where they are wanted and builds what you lay out

+roster.name: Woodcutter
+roster.desc: Works at a woodcutter's hut: fells the trees round it and leaves the logs there for the carriers

+roster.name: Stone Cutter
+roster.desc: Works at a quarry: cuts the stone round it and leaves it there for the carriers

+roster.name: Sawyer
+roster.desc: Works at a sawmill: saws logs into planks

+roster.name: Farmer
+roster.desc: Works at a farm: sows its wheat fields, reaps them once ripe and leaves the grain there for the serfs

+roster.name: Miller
+roster.desc: Works at a mill: grinds grain into flour

+roster.name: Baker
+roster.desc: Works at a bakery: bakes flour into bread

+roster.name: Miner
+roster.desc: Works at a mine: digs the seam behind it and leaves the ore for the carriers

+roster.name: Smelter
+roster.desc: Works at a smelter: melts ore with coal into iron bars or gold

+roster.name: Smith
+roster.desc: Works at a smithy: forges iron and planks into tools

+roster.name: Swineherd
+roster.desc: Works at a pig farm: fattens pigs on grain

+roster.name: Butcher
+roster.desc: Works at a butcher's: makes pigs into sausages

+roster.name: Winegrower
+roster.desc: Works at a vineyard: picks the grapes on its vines and presses them into wine outside it
